title: Longest Repeating Character Replacement
summary: Given a string s and an integer k , you can change any character in the string to any other uppercase English letter at most k times.
statement: Given a string s and an integer k , you can change any character in the string to any other uppercase English letter at most k times. Determine the length of the longest substring that can be made to contain the same character throughout, after performing these changes.
constraints: 1 <= s.length <= 100,000; uppercase English letters only; 0 <= k <= s.length.
Change at most k characters to any uppercase letter. Return the longest contiguous substring that can become one repeated letter.
Choose the target letter freely; you do not need to return or mutate the string.
reference_solution:
def longest_replaced_run(s, k):
    counts = [0]*26
    left = largest = best = 0
    for right,char in enumerate(s):
        index = ord(char)-ord('A')
        counts[index] += 1
        largest = max(largest,counts[index])
        if right-left+1-largest>k:
            counts[ord(s[left])-ord('A')] -= 1
            left += 1
        best = max(best,right-left+1)
    return best

hints: For a fixed window, keep its most frequent letter and replace the rest.
Grow a sliding window while its size minus the best letter frequency fits the budget.
Increment the newest letter, update historical largest frequency, and shift left once when window size minus largest exceeds k.
A historical maximum can leave an invalid current window, but cannot create a larger false record: growth needs a genuinely increased frequency. This version returns only the best length.
editorial: A window of length L needs L-max_frequency replacements. Track 26 counts and a nondecreasing historical maximum. Window length never decreases: it either grows or shifts at constant size. A stale frequency may preserve an already achieved length, but growing past that record requires a new real frequency large enough to support it. Thus the maximum length is correct even though this optimized variant must not be used to return an arbitrary current window as a witness.
